newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU issues telecoms "universal service" guidelines.
newsitem.headline: EU issues telecoms "universal service" guidelines.

text.p: The European Commission issued guidelines on Wednesday aimed at ensuring that governments do not stifle competition in the telecommunications sector by imposing unfair costs on new operators.

The communication(*) -- issued in the run-up to the January 1, 1998 EU deadline for opening telecoms markets to competition -- applies to national schemes for raising money to finance "universal service", or affordable basic phone service to all residents.

EU legislation allows governments to ask certain telecoms operators to contribute to the cost of providing universal service -- for example, voice telephone, fax and directory assistance -- once the traditional phone companies lose their monopolies.
They may ask them to contribute to a "universal service fund" or to pay special fees known as "supplementary charges" when they hook up to telecoms networks of universal service providers.
But the Commission said such schemes must meet the following criteria:

-- In line with the draft Interconnection Directive, COM(95)379, only companies providing public telecoms networks or public voice telephone services may be asked to contribute. The contributions may be imposed on voice telephone providers only in proportion to their usage of public networks.
The Commission may allow governments to require mobile phone operators to contribute if they can justify it.
-- Companies operating corporate telecoms networks, data communications services or enhanced voice telephone services such as videoconferencing or voice mail may not be asked to contribute.

-- The money may only cover unavoidable net losses incurred by an operator in providing public fixed telephone networks and services. The calculation should cover customers who would be disconnected if the operator were acting solely on commercial grounds.
-- The schemes may not cover obligations outside the scope of universal service -- for example, public security measures, normal network modernisation or itemised billing.

-- Universal service funds must be administered by an independent body that is responsible for collecting contributions. Supplementary charges should be calculated by the operators concerned in a transparent and non-discriminatory way that is subject to review by national regulatory authorities.

-- Companies should contribute money according to the size of their activity on the relevant market. The schemes should include procedures for clearly identifying the market on which such activity is measured.

EU states must submit their plans for Commission approval before January 11, 1997. (*) "Commission Communication on assessment criteria for national schemes for the costing and financing of universal service in telecommunications and guidelines for the member states on operation of such schemes"
